_comment: Shard definitions for test projects too large to run as a single unit.
A package listed here has its test suite split into shards; a package that
is not listed runs as one unit. Shards are crossed with the tier filters
(deterministic / coyote / chaos) by plan-test-matrix.py, so a shard is a
slice of a project's tests and a tier is a slice of a shard.
ORDERED FIRST-MATCH-WINS. Shards are evaluated top to bottom and a test
belongs to the FIRST shard whose include prefixes match it. The generated
filter for shard i is therefore OR(its own includes) AND NOT(includes of
every earlier shard). This is what makes the list a PARTITION rather than
an allow-list: every test lands in exactly one shard, so a suite cannot
silently lose coverage to a gap between two patterns, and two shards
cannot both claim the same test and run it twice.
The ordering is load-bearing. 'BPlusTree.ChaosPredicate' must precede
'BPlusTree.Chaos', which must precede 'BPlusTree.', because each is a
prefix of the one before it. Put a broad prefix above a narrow one and the
narrow shard silently runs nothing - which is why the leg summary reports
the executed test count per shard and the aggregate report flags any shard
that ran zero tests in every tier.
The final shard must set "complement": true. It matches everything no
earlier shard claimed, so adding a new test namespace can never fall
outside the partition and go untested.
Prefixes are relative to namespaceRoot and are matched against the VSTest
FullyQualifiedName, which is Namespace.Class.Method. A trailing dot pins
the match to a namespace segment ('Grains.'); no trailing dot lets it
match a class-name prefix ('ChaosPredicate'), which is how the chaos
fixtures that all share one namespace are split.
CROSSING WITH TIERS IS OPTIONAL. By default a sharded package's shards are
crossed with the deterministic / coyote / chaos filters, so each shard
becomes three invocations. That pays off only when the tiers are
independently large enough to fill separate runners, which is true of
'lattice' and of nothing else so far. A package whose suite carries no
Chaos and no Coyote category at all sets "crossTiers": false and gets one
untiered invocation per shard instead, saving two empty process starts per
shard. It is safe against a future fixture because it removes the tier
filter rather than naming the tiers to keep: the shard expressions are
still a partition, so a new Chaos test lands in a shard and runs.

Smaller cross-cutting areas grouped into one shard.

The TLC mutation gates are CPU-bound JVM runs, so they are split across their own shards by the TlcShard* category test/lattice/Formal/TlcCiShard.cs gives each case (a category, because the NUnit adapter's filter parser rejects a FullName prefix that ends inside a case's argument list). Each shard runs several cases at a time, so its item time is a fraction of its summed case time. This shard holds every Replication EventualConvergence (temporal) mutant: 9 cases, 13.6 case-minutes in a 4.05-minute item in the receipt-free bucket push run 40909619830 (#5166). Mutants sharing a target property and options share one cached control (#5152); the Replication base runs in formal-tlc-replication-wal, so these mutants still launch that control here.

MaterialisedViewTail base, ThreeWrites variant and 22 mutants: all 24 cases measured at 342s on Java 17 with two visible CPUs and one TLC slot. Mutants sharing a target property and options share one cached control (#5152). Staging companions require separate measured groups when enrolled.

MaterialisedViewFence base, NewerOrdinary and nine paired mutants: 11/11 cases, zero skips. Final one-JVM/two-CPU/Xmx2g no-build command measured 48.434s; that figure predates control sharing by content (#5152) and includes one control per mutant.

MaterialisedViewHorizon base, FullScan and twenty-three paired mutants: 25/25 cases, zero skipped, inconclusive or not-executed. Final one-JVM/two-CPU/Xmx2g no-build command measured 196.4s over three distinct prepare/terminal partitions, retained-cardinality witnesses and abandoned recovery.

MaterialisedViewAggregation base, Delete and eighteen paired mutants: 20/20 cases, zero skips. Independent one-JVM/two-CPU/1800MB no-build command measured 95.417s (a figure that predates control sharing by content (#5152) and includes one control per mutant); numeric membership, partial public repair and history revisions.

MaterialisedViewRebind base, NoCrash and twenty paired mutants: 22/22 cases, zero skips. Independent one-JVM/two-CPU/1800MB no-build command measured 117.545s (a figure that predates control sharing by content (#5152) and includes one control per mutant); captured source/floor publication, late alias movement and simultaneous bound/candidate floor protection.

ReadyClosure base, History, TwoConsumers and twelve paired mutants: 15/15 cases, zero skips. Independent one-JVM/two-CPU/1800MiB no-build command measured 94.200s (a figure that predates control sharing by content (#5152) and includes one control per mutant); independent clocks, transitive replacement closure, external eligibility hold and per-consumer atomic snapshots.

SourceAdmission base, CrossTree, History, PendingSource, PendingOverlay and twenty-one paired mutants: 26/26 cases, zero skips. One-JVM/two-CPU/1800MiB no-build command measured 239.838s (a figure that predates control sharing by content (#5152) and includes one control per mutant); logical pending-row/decision identity, source-apply lag, omission entitlement and expected-participant closure. The duration table prices this measured expanded population at 4.00 minutes.

ResolvedIdentity base, SameLog, FailedCandidate, LostCandidate and sixteen paired mutants: 20/20 cases, zero skips. Independent one-JVM/two-CPU/1800MiB no-build command measured 61.385s; actual-tail cache ownership, reused transaction IDs, same-log rebuild and uncertain publication responses.

Fresh joint-repair base, Legacy, SingleTarget and TwoFaults variants, and 25 typed mutation/control pairs: all 29 cases measured at 97.221 seconds including VSTest startup on Java 17, two visible CPUs and one TLC slot. Isolated from the existing materialised-view tail work; bounded two-participant repair, automatic historical completion cleanup and durable acknowledgement closure.

Schema-independent numeric (Count/Sum) projection companion: MaterialisedViewNumeric base, Swap and TwoFaults variants and twenty paired mutations, 23 cases, measured at 1.43 minutes on its leg in receipt-free ci.yml run 41064780376 (head ff6cc0c64), where every TLC module ran exhaustively. Extraction and encoding, durable publication obligations, operation identity, filter-version and physical-copy rebind.

Shared durable alias routing and cutover interactions, retaining same-property controls with their mutations.

Resize/undo, grow/shrink reshard and shadow-cutover composition base, repeated-crash variant and mutants: 50 cases measured at 99.2s with Java 17, two visible CPUs and one TLC slot. Mutants sharing a target property and options share one cached control (#5152).

The ReplayPermits TwoPartitions variant remains in a dedicated one-case shard: it is the longest indivisible TLC case and so sets the cold critical path. Its measured item took 35.22 minutes in the receipt-free bucket push ci.yml run 40909619830 (head 9418a498d, job 123577568395) and 52.78 in coverage.yml run 40923724192 (head 0e4aa6b2a, job 123623834893); 44.00 is their mean, a planning input, not a future runtime guarantee. It remains separate from the other scheduling groups.

Every SchemaPolicyConfig, SchemaStageOrdering, SchemaVersionFamily, SchemaDurableOperation, SchemaComplianceScan and SchemaStrictIngest base, variant and mutation (104 cases), bases co-located with their mutations so the base runs serve the full-bound controls. The first two modules' 30 cases took 2.34 minutes (dotnet test 2 m 17 s) in the member pull request ci.yml run 41065598921 (head 675f6363f, job 124100785054) for #5226; with SchemaVersionFamily, 48 took 1 m 54 s of dotnet test in ci.yml run 41087582284 (head e15b3091e, job 124175924963) for #5227; with SchemaDurableOperation and SchemaComplianceScan instead, 68 took 6.64 minutes (dotnet test 6 m 34 s) in ci.yml run 41088681728 (head 4e5554713, job 124180139236) for #5229. The SchemaDurableOperation ThreeOps variant and its three-operation mutation controls dominate, then the SchemaPolicyConfig ThreeSilos variant. The 18 SchemaStrictIngest cases took 0.78 minutes locally (16-core Windows workstation, default TLC concurrency) for #5228; refresh from that member pull request run. Split the shard from measured timings as further Schema* modules join it.

Every TLC case not already claimed: bases not co-located with their mutations (TlcCiShard.CoLocatedBaseCategory lists the moved ones; ShardOwnership and BackupCapture stay here), ungrouped variants, mutations of ungrouped modules (including BPlusTopology), and synthetic-module gates. The lifecycle, materialised-view and anti-entropy areas route their bases, variants and mutants together above this catch-all. 159 cases, 61.0 case-minutes in a 17.34-minute item in the receipt-free bucket push run 40909619830 (#5166), led by the WalDurability SnapshotLoss variant (9.6 minutes). It selects by name prefix rather than by category, so it keeps every tier: a non-TLC fixture under that prefix must not lose its Chaos or Coyote tier.
